cohort: The study comprised 280 pregnant subjects who underwent a 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test and an evaluation of glycated haemoglobin.
finding: Glycated haemoglobin levels were significantly different between pregnant subjects with and without gestational diabetes mellitus, showing a sensitivity of 70% and specificity of 84.78% for diagnosis.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, between January 2016 and January 2018.
